title: Sensitive Paths
description: Input to the risk-registry modifier `target_matches_sensitive_path` (F2): raises an action's risk score by what the action TOUCHES, not only by what the action is called.

governs.description: Which plane this policy governs (C10). Sensitivity scoring is an assistant-plane concern.

enforce_at_pretooluse.description: Turn on HARD enforcement in the PreToolUse guard. Ships false: enabling it changes runtime behaviour for every session in that project, so it is opted into per project rather than inherited from the bundle.

enforced_at.description: Where this file is actually consumed today. Declaring a stronger value than reality is the failure C10 exists to prevent.

default_score_delta.description: Applied when a rule omits score_delta. Must be large enough to cross into a tier whose approver is not the default role — see why_delta_is_60.

exclude_globs.description: Paths that match `globs` but must NOT escalate. Checked after globs; an exclusion wins. Added from real measurement, not theory: the first scan of a live repo escalated a test file, an ADR that discusses secrets, and .env.example — none of which is the thing the rule is guarding.

approvable.description: P1 1.0: a write blocked by this rule may be approved through the Portal (needs approval_path.enabled). Default false: opt-in per rule.

reason.description: Why this path is sensitive. A rule nobody can justify is a rule that gets deleted the first time it is inconvenient.

approval_path.description: P1 1.0: lets a blocked write be approved in Portal Approvals (one file, one use, time-limited) instead of only hard-blocked. Absent or enabled=false means hard-block only.
